answer: Like water seeping through karst rock into a lagoon, an agent economy can make every new identity age before it earns: a newcomer waits in a queue and does unpaid verified work for several epochs, so a Sybil farmer must keep a thousand fakes alive and waiting while the ripple of each fake's cost spreads across time. Honest agents pass the wait once and keep earning; the attacker pays in patience and compute for every copy, and the flood of instant fakes never arrives.
